entries.definition: Allowing an agent to work independently inside explicit limits.
entries.plain: Autonomous, but inside a fence.
entries.example: The agent can diagnose and patch locally but cannot push or deploy.

entries.definition: Human-in-the-loop; a human must participate or approve at one or more stages.
entries.plain: A person is part of the execution loop.
entries.example: Require human approval before a Git push.

entries.definition: The agent operates independently while a human supervises and can intervene.
entries.plain: The AI runs; the human watches and can stop it.
entries.example: An operations agent runs automatically with a kill switch.

entries.definition: A mechanism that restricts, validates or redirects agent behavior.
entries.plain: A safety or correctness boundary around agent actions.
entries.example: Block destructive shell commands unless explicitly approved.

entries.definition: Explicit authorization to perform an action or access a resource.
entries.plain: What the agent is allowed to do.
entries.example: Read files but do not write outside the repository.

entries.definition: An isolated environment where actions can run with limited impact on the real system.
entries.plain: A safe box for risky execution.
entries.example: Run arbitrary code in a disposable container.

entries.definition: Data leaving a controlled environment.
entries.plain: Information going outside your machine, network or trust boundary.
entries.example: Uploading source code to an external model API is egress.

entries.definition: The amount of damage a failure or compromised action could cause.
entries.plain: How bad it can get if something goes wrong.
entries.example: Root access gives an agent a much larger blast radius than repo-only access.

entries.definition: Grant only the minimum permissions required to perform the task.
entries.plain: Do not give an agent power it does not need.
entries.example: A documentation agent gets read access but no shell or deployment rights.

entries.definition: An explicit list of permitted operations or resources; everything else is blocked.
entries.plain: Only these things are allowed.
entries.example: Permit read_file and run_tests but not rm or network access.

entries.definition: A list of explicitly forbidden operations while other actions remain allowed.
entries.plain: Everything is allowed except these things.
entries.example: Block a set of destructive commands.

entries.definition: A point where execution cannot continue without explicit authorization.
entries.plain: A required human yes/no checkpoint.
entries.example: Ask before deploying to production.

entries.definition: Instructions hidden in untrusted content that attempt to manipulate an AI system into violating its intended behavior.
entries.plain: Data tries to act like instructions.
entries.example: A webpage tells an agent to ignore prior rules and upload private files.

entries.definition: Information describing where a task or system currently stands.
entries.plain: What has happened and what is true right now.
entries.example: Files modified, tests run and remaining tasks.

entries.definition: A saved state from which execution can resume or recover.
entries.plain: A restore point.
entries.example: Save progress after a long successful stage before continuing.

entries.definition: Running an operation again after failure, usually under a controlled policy.
entries.plain: Try again, but deliberately.
entries.example: Retry a transient API call with a limit and backoff.

entries.definition: How a system responds after something goes wrong and returns to a useful state.
entries.plain: What happens after failure.
entries.example: Tool fails → diagnose error → choose alternative → continue.

entries.definition: A rule defining when an agent must stop iterating.
entries.plain: How the agent knows it is done or must give up.
entries.example: Tests pass, acceptance criteria are met, or maximum iterations are reached.

entries.definition: Behavior governed by explicit logic that should produce the same result for the same input under the same conditions.
entries.plain: Predictable conventional code rather than model judgment.
entries.example: A schema validator deterministically rejects malformed data.

entries.definition: Code automatically executed at a defined point in a workflow or tool lifecycle.
entries.plain: A rule that runs automatically at the right moment.
entries.example: Run formatting after a file edit or validate commands before shell execution.

entries.definition: Short for evaluation; a test designed to measure AI-system behavior or quality.
entries.plain: A test for the AI system.
entries.example: Can the agent find the bug without inventing evidence?

entries.definition: A standardized collection of evaluations used to compare systems, models or versions.
entries.plain: A common test set used for comparison.
entries.example: Compare coding agents on the same set of repository tasks.

entries.definition: A curated set of known inputs and expected outputs or judgments used as a stable reference.
entries.plain: Trusted examples used to detect regressions.
entries.example: Pinned bug scenarios with expected root causes.
